problem_fingerprint.source: Bansal–Jiang–Meka–Singla–Sinha, arXiv:2111.07049v1, §1 definition and §6 Open Problem 6.1; independently restated by Karingula–Lovett, ECCC TR26-188, Conjecture 1.6.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: There exists a finite universal C such that for every positive integer d, every positive integer T, and every ordered sequence v1,...,vT in R^d of Euclidean norm at most one, there exists one sign vector epsilon in {−1,+1}^T.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Real vectors, Euclidean input norm ≤1; coordinate maximum output norm.
problem_fingerprint.order_and_information: The order is prescribed and cannot be permuted. Signs may depend on the entire sequence; no online or efficient-algorithm requirement.
problem_fingerprint.simultaneity: The same signs must control every prefix and coordinate, with C independent of dimension, sequence length, and data.
problem_fingerprint.family: One canonical all-dimension prefix-signing question; related norm/sparsity versions receive no extra count.

indirect_implication_checks: Separate terminal signings for different prefixes need not agree. Stacking all prefix constraints duplicates v_i in T-i+1 coordinate blocks, making its Euclidean norm sqrt(T-i+1) times larger; normalization loses the desired constant.
Making all vectors small enough for H26 by scaling and then rescaling restores a length-dependent bound. Its displayed failure estimate need not be below one without smallness.
A discarded-term guarantee does not ensure zero discards at a fixed universal radius. Complex phases are a larger feasible class than real signs.
Online lower bounds reverse the information quantifiers: a fixed sequence may have good offline signs despite defeating every online strategy.

applied_significance: In a two-group allocation interpretation, epsilon assigns each whole vector and each prefix sum measures cumulative feature/resource imbalance. Equivalently x_i=(1+epsilon_i)/2 rounds a half-allocation with error one-half the displayed discrepancy. BJMSS22 §1 links prefix discrepancy to Steinitz bounds, integer programming and scheduling; no efficient construction follows merely from existence.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: AA26 Theorem 2 gives O(sqrt(log(2T))) for arbitrary fixed inputs at fixed positive success probability. BJMSS22 also records O(d) uniformly in T. Neither is independent of both parameters; H26 provides a constant for sufficiently small coordinates.

proposed_statement:
Does there exist an absolute constant $C>0$ with the following property? For every pair of positive integers $d,T$ and every ordered sequence $v_1,\ldots,v_T\in\mathbb R^d$ with Euclidean norms $\|v_i\|_2\le1$, one can choose signs $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_T\in\{-1,1\}$ such that

$$
\max_{1\le k\le T}
\left\|\sum_{i=1}^{k}\varepsilon_i v_i\right\|_\infty
\le C,
\qquad
\|z\|_\infty=\max_{1\le j\le d}|z_j|?
$$

The order is fixed. The signs may depend on the entire sequence, but the same signs must work for every prefix and coordinate. The constant must be independent of $d$, $T$ and the vectors. This is the strong, or prefix, Komlós conjecture. No online decision rule or efficient algorithm is required. [1, 2]

Taking $k=T$ gives the ordinary terminal-sum question in [entry 031](../../../problems/031-komlos.md). Controlling each prefix with a separately chosen signing would not answer the stronger question here.
